Step 2, the pilot: two paintings

Pilot painting prompts

Two paintings to make in ChatGPT before any others: the fair square for walking, and the moor clearing for fights. Each prompt comes with a grey-box picture drawn from the game's own camera, so the painting comes back already lined up.

When these two are in, I fit them, put the Jester in them, and you judge the look. The other twelve wait until then.

How to run it

  1. Look at the two labelled layouts below. If a layout is not what you want, tell me before you paint anything.
  2. Save the four images to attach. They are on this page, and in the zip I sent in the chat.
  3. Start a new ChatGPT chat for each painting. Attach its three images in the order given, then paste its prompt.
  4. Make each one two to four times. Keep the one whose layout matches the guide best, even if another is prettier.
  5. Save the keepers as W1.png and F1.png. A second keeper is W1b.png. Send them back as they come, with no squeezing.

The four images to attach

Press and hold a picture to save it, or use the zip from the chat.

W1: The fair square

The first walking scene: the game starts here. It is twice as wide as it is tall so the screen can pan across it as she walks.

  • KindWalking scene
  • ShapeWide, 2:1, 2048 x 1024 or larger
  • Attach, in this orderG1, then P1, then S1
  • Save asW1.png
Prompt W1
One production background painting for my fantasy role-playing game, Moon Faire. The game draws realistic 3D characters on top of this painting, walking on its ground.

Output exactly ONE landscape image, 2:1 (twice as wide as it is tall), 2048 x 1024 pixels or larger. Not a collage or a contact sheet.

I am attaching three images.
- Image 1 is the CAMERA AND LAYOUT GUIDE: a grey-box model of this exact scene, drawn from the exact camera the game uses. Keep its camera, its perspective and its layout. Every tent, stall, lantern post, the well, the round square and the two lanes stay where the guide puts them and the size the guide makes them. Take only layout, scale and the direction of the light from it. Do not copy its grey colours or its blocky shapes: paint real things in their places. The bright magenta figure is a measuring marker 1.70 m tall, the height of a person here. Use it for scale, then leave it out and paint the bare ground where it stands.
- Image 2 is a finished background painting from another game of mine. Match its craft and finish. Take nothing else from it: not its place, not its camera, not its night colours.
- Image 3 is one of the characters who will stand in this scene, shown from the front and the back. It is there to show how realistic the characters are. Never paint her, or anyone, into the scene.

VIEW. As in Image 1: a high three-quarter view, looking down at about 24 degrees through a long lens, like the painted backgrounds of classic role-playing games. The perspective is flattened: things at the back are only a little smaller than things at the front, and upright things stay upright. Not isometric, not straight down.

STYLE. A realistic, richly detailed, hand-painted scene with believable scale and painterly but detailed surfaces: real canvas, rope, wood, stone, earth and grass. It has to sit behind realistic 3D characters, so paint it as real as Image 3. Not pixel art, not a cartoon, not anime, no drawn outlines, not game tiles.

LIGHT. The game's characters are always lit the same way, so every painting in this set is lit the same way:
- The main light is warm and soft. It comes from behind the viewer and from the right, a little under 45 degrees up. The sides of things that face the viewer and the right are the lit sides. Soft shadows fall away from the viewer and to the left, toward the upper left of the picture, about as long as the thing is tall. Image 1 shows this.
- The moon, Auros, is behind the scene in the upper left of the sky. It edges the upper-left outlines of things with cool, pale lilac light. It does not cast the main shadows.
- A cool blue-violet sky light fills the shadows from low on the left. Shadows are soft and never black.
- The ground is warm in colour: earth, dry grass and warm stone.
- Only lit lanterns, the moon and the sky are bright. Everything else is calm enough that a brightly dressed character stands out against it.

LEAVE OUT, because the game draws them live on top: people, animals and creatures of any kind; the magenta marker; fireflies, moths, drifting smoke, sparks, glows of magic, rain and lightning. No lettering anywhere: signs and banners are blank or patterned. No captions, labels, borders, UI, grid lines or vignette.

GROUND THE CHARACTERS WALK ON. The round square, both lanes and the open ground between the tents are level, clear and easy to read. Nothing hangs over them or hides them: no roof, awning, banner, rope, branch or string of flags crosses walkable ground. Do not string bunting or flags across the square: the game adds its own. Every tent door and every stall front that faces the square is fully visible. Keep the middle of the square empty except for what the guide shows.

THE SCENE: THE FAIR SQUARE AT DUSK.
The middle of the Moon Faire, a travelling fair of tents that follows the moon across the world, in a dark-ages fantasy land. People of many lands travel with it, so its tents and stalls are a mix of cloths, patterns and crafts from many cultures. It is dusk and the lanterns have just been lit.
- The ground: a round square about 14 m across of pale, trodden earth, edged by a ring of worn flat stones. A trodden earth lane, about 4 m wide, leaves the square to the left edge of the picture, and another to the right edge.
- In the square, toward the back: a performer's floor cloth lying flat on the ground, a rug about 4.5 m by 3 m in deep red with a gold border, with four small brass footlights along each short side. It is completely flat: no stage and no platform.
- In the square, front right of the middle: a small round stone well with a low wall, two wooden posts, a little shingled roof and a bucket.
- Eight lantern posts round the square, exactly where the guide puts them: dark wooden posts 3.3 m tall, each with one lit lantern of warm amber glass that throws a small warm pool of light on the ground.
- Tents and stalls where the guide's boxes stand. Back left, a round tent in broad wine-red and cream stripes with a pointed roof. Back middle, two open market stalls with cloth awnings and wooden counters. Back right, a square tent of indigo cloth with a pale star pattern. On the left, above the lane, a square tent of ochre and rust cloth; below the lane, an open stall. On the right, above the lane, an open stall; below the lane, a round tent of green and gold cloth. Each tent has its door flap toward the square, and each stall its counter. Their colours are rich but softened by the dusk.
- At the bottom corners of the picture, the tops of two more tents frame the scene, as in the guide.
- Along the front: a painted wooden wagon on the left, and a stack of crates and barrels on the right, as in the guide.
- The top of the picture is a narrow band, as in the guide. Beyond the tents stands the fair's big top with its two peaks, dark against the sky, with more tent tops and a far line of low hills. The sky is deep blue-violet above, with a last low band of rose and amber. Auros, the moon, is large, pale and nearly full, exactly where the guide puts it in the upper left.

Prompt F1
One production background painting for my fantasy role-playing game, Moon Faire: the backdrop of a battle. The game draws realistic 3D characters, creatures and spell effects on top of it, standing on the open ground across the bottom.

Output exactly ONE landscape 4:3 image, 2048 x 1536 pixels or larger. Not a collage or a contact sheet.

I am attaching three images.
- Image 1 is the CAMERA AND LAYOUT GUIDE: a grey-box model of this exact scene, drawn from the exact camera the game uses. Keep its camera, its horizon, its moon and its layout. Take only layout, scale and the direction of the light from it. Do not copy its grey colours or its blocky shapes: paint real things in their places. The bright magenta figure is a measuring marker 1.70 m tall, standing where a character will stand. Use it for scale, then leave it out and paint the bare ground where it stands.
- Image 2 is a finished battle background from another game of mine, painted for the same camera. Match its craft, its finish, its believable scale and the way haze separates its layers. Do not copy its place, its mountains or its cold colours.
- Image 3 is one of the characters who will stand in this scene, shown from the front and the back. It is there to show how realistic the characters are. Never paint her, or anyone, into the scene.

VIEW. As in Image 1: a camera near eye level, tilted very slightly up, with a 38-degree lens feel. The horizon is level and sits 61% of the way down the picture. A flat, wide, open clearing fills the bottom third.

STYLE. A realistic, richly detailed, hand-painted scene with believable scale and painterly but detailed surfaces: real canvas, rope, wood, stone, earth and grass. It has to sit behind realistic 3D characters, so paint it as real as Image 3. Not pixel art, not a cartoon, not anime, no drawn outlines, not game tiles.

LIGHT. The game's characters are always lit the same way, so every painting in this set is lit the same way:
- The main light is warm and soft. It comes from behind the viewer and from the right, a little under 45 degrees up. The sides of things that face the viewer and the right are the lit sides. Soft shadows fall away from the viewer and to the left, toward the upper left of the picture, about as long as the thing is tall. Image 1 shows this.
- The moon, Auros, is behind the scene in the upper left of the sky. It edges the upper-left outlines of things with cool, pale lilac light. It does not cast the main shadows.
- A cool blue-violet sky light fills the shadows from low on the left. Shadows are soft and never black.
- The ground is warm in colour: earth, dry grass and warm stone.
- Only lit lanterns, the moon and the sky are bright. Everything else is calm enough that a brightly dressed character stands out against it.

LEAVE OUT, because the game draws them live on top: people, animals and creatures of any kind; the magenta marker; fireflies, moths, drifting smoke, sparks, glows of magic, rain and lightning. No lettering anywhere: signs and banners are blank or patterned. No captions, labels, borders, UI, grid lines or vignette.

THE OPEN GROUND. The bottom third of the picture is entirely level, unobstructed ground, calm and low in contrast, lit softly and evenly, with its detail getting smaller toward the horizon. The game stands its characters here and adds its own moving grass. Nothing stands on it: no rocks, water, paths, roots, walls, posts, props or steps, and no trees or branches framing the foreground. Everything with a shape of its own is in the middle distance or far away, behind the clearing.

THE SCENE: THE MOOR CLEARING AT NIGHT.
A moonlit moor a short walk beyond the Moon Faire, a travelling fair of tents, in a dark-ages fantasy land.
- The clearing: short moor grass with low heather and dry bracken, in warm, muted greens, tans and dusty purples. It is night, but the clearing reads clearly.
- Far off on the left of the horizon, small, as in the guide: the warm glow of the fair's lanterns and the dark double peak of its big top, with a few smaller tent tops beside it. It is tiny and distant.
- In the middle distance, beyond the clearing: an old road of worn flagstones that runs behind the clearing and curves away to the right toward the horizon; a low dry-stone wall on the left; clumps of gorse and heather; one wind-bent thorn tree right of the middle; and a leaning waymark stone beside the road on the right. None of them comes forward into the clearing.
- Far away: low rolling moor hills in two or three hazy bands, as in the guide. No mountains. Thin silver-lavender haze lies between the layers.
- The sky: a broad, calm night sky in deep plum and indigo, with a few faint stars and thin wisps of cloud. Auros, the moon, is large, bright, detailed and nearly full, with a soft glow round it, exactly where the guide puts it: 31% of the way across and 17% of the way down, about 13% of the picture's height across.

Before you keep one

Both

  • No people, creatures or magenta figure anywhere.
  • No lettering, labels or borders.
  • Painted and realistic: not pixel art, not a cartoon.
  • Auros is in the upper left, where the guide has it.
  • Lit sides face the viewer and the right; shadows fall up and to the left.

W1, the fair square

  • The tents, stalls, posts and well stand where the guide's boxes are.
  • The square is the same flattened oval as the guide, and both lanes reach the picture's edges.
  • You can see the ground everywhere a witch could walk: nothing hangs over it.
  • The floor cloth lies flat. No stage.
  • No bunting strung across the square.

F1, the moor clearing

  • The horizon is level and about 61% of the way down.
  • The bottom third is flat, open and empty.
  • The fair is tiny and far off on the left.
  • The road, wall, tree and stone all stay behind the clearing.

What I chose, for you to check

  • The two cameras are Envoi's, because they already work with paintings: the night square's for walking (a long lens looking down at 24 degrees) and the arena's for fights (2 m up, 18 m back, the horizon 61% down).
  • Auros has one fixed spot in every fight backdrop (31% across, 17% down, as in Envoi) and one in every walking scene (the upper left of the top band).
  • A person is about a tenth of the walking painting's height. On screen the game shows about two thirds of the painting's width, so she is about a seventh of the screen's height.
  • In a fight a witch is about a seventh of the backdrop's height in the wide shot. Closer shots are crops of the same picture.
  • What is in the square is my guess at a fair: the tents' colours, the well, the wagon. The Jester's floor cloth comes from the earlier plan. Change any words in the scene part of a prompt.
  • I asked for 2048 pixels wide. ChatGPT gave you 1448 and 1536 wide for Envoi. Either is enough to fit and judge the pilot.
